Hi Stephanie,

- Liability: remove or materially increase the liability cap; we cannot accept the current cap tied to fees for our use case.

We also attached an internal procurement timeline — we need final contract terms and a signed SOW by July 14 to hit the onboarding window. Can Redwood accommodate these points or propose defensible alternatives?

Steph / team — reviewed the redlines. Commercial summary and recommendation below: 

- Pricing: Elysium asks for 35% off. Recommend a structured compromise: 25% off for a 12-month committed pilot, or 20% with a shorter 6-mo pilot + expansion credit. We should keep the discount tied to ARR ramp / committed seats.
- Liability: they want to "remove" the cap. Not acceptable. For a strategic pilot we can consider raising our standard cap but cap should remain finite — propose a one-time exception to $1.5M (subject to exec sign-off).
- Indemnity: their requested broad IP + data indemnity is risky. Offer limited IP indemnity for third-party claims for model outputs (standard carveouts) and keep data-related claims limited to Redwood's gross negligence or willful misconduct.

Attached: negotiation_playbook.pdf — includes fallback language and customer QBR talking points.

Commercially I’m in favor of making this a priority — Elysium has good logos and a chance to expand. If legal signs off on a $1.5M cap and tight indemnity carveouts, I recommend we move forward with the 25%/12-mo option. This will likely require Marissa or the CRO to approve.

Subject: Re: Elysium pilot — contract redlines and SOW (legal review)

Team — I read the redlines and James Park’s notes. High-level legal position and risks: 

1) Broad indemnity for "data-related claims" is not acceptable. We should not assume liability for Elysium’s downstream customer data practices. Suggest we carve data claims out from any indemnity except where they directly result from Redwood's breach of data security obligations or willful misconduct.

2) IP indemnity: we can offer a limited IP indemnity for infringement claims caused by our deliverables, subject to (a) prompt notice, (b) sole defense control by Redwood, and (c) use within scope. We must exclude claims arising from customer-supplied prompts or third-party model components used by the customer.

3) Liability cap: our standard is the greater of $1M or fees paid in 12 months (commonly limited). Given the pilot size, I can support a one-time exception to up to $1.25M for a strategic customer, but anything above $1.25M requires executive (CRO + CEO) approval after a short business case. 

4) Warranty: we can accept a limited warranty tied to the SOW deliverables and security controls, but we cannot extend uptime SLAs beyond what our infra guarantees without capacity commitments.

Action items: 
- If commercial wants to push to $1.5M liability, we need a written exec approval that documents the upside and mitigation steps.
- If team wants to accept broader indemnity language, require re-drafted clauses that narrow scope and include caps/exclusions.

Attaching a short legal_risk_summary.pdf. I recommend we present two options to execs:

Option A (recommended): 25% discount / 12-mo pilot; liability cap exception to $1.25M; tighten indemnity carveouts to the language I propose in the attached.
Option B: 20% discount / 12-mo + escalation clause; liability cap up to $1.5M only with documented exec approval and additional commercial concessions (higher fees or escrow).

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com

Marissa — requesting executive approval / guidance. Summary and ask below.

Summary: Elysium (pilot customer) has submitted redlines that request an effectively uncapped liability and broad indemnity for IP and data claims, plus a 35% discount. Commercial believes Elysium is strategically valuable and recommends a compromise; Legal has flagged material risk and has limited the liability exception we can approve without exec sign-off.

Key documents attached: Elysium_SOW_v3_redlines.pdf (original redlines), risk_matrix.xlsx (internal impact), negotiation_playbook.pdf (commercial fallback language), legal_risk_summary.pdf. DocuSign link for the current SOW is: https://www.docusign.net/ELY-2026-SOW-sign (internal).

Decision requested: please provide a one-line approval for one of the two options below or request a short sync with CEO + CRO if you prefer. We need a decision by end of day Monday, July 6 to meet Elysium’s procurement window.

Option A — Recommended (fastest path):
- Approve 25% introductory discount for a 12-month committed pilot.
- Approve one-time liability cap exception to $1.25M (legal to reword indemnity carveouts; Redwood controls defense for IP claims).
- Require customer to accept the proposed narrow indemnity carveouts for data claims (Redwood only liable for direct damages from our proven breach).

Option B — Premium concession (requires higher-level sign-off):
- Approve 25% discount + additional commercial concessions (e.g., reduced ramp fees) in exchange for $1.5M liability cap.
- Escalate to CRO + CEO for explicit written approval; include mitigation plan (insurance check, implementation milestones).

Recommended next step if approved: Lauren to issue a revised mark with exact clause language; Ben to send a revised commercial term sheet; I will coordinate to get countersigned.

Requested sign-off: Marissa Cole or designate (CRO/CEO) — please reply with one-line approval or call-out changes.

Thanks — I’m available for a 20-min sync any time tomorrow.
